subtype: Approach: avoid the appointment hoping it will pass [Pitfall]
passage:
Chetan: Did you go for the check-up?
Karthik: Not yet
Karthik: Demo on Thursday, after that I will
Chetan: You said that two weeks ago
Karthik: Ha. The viva is next week though
Karthik: If it was serious I'd know by now, right? 🤞
Chetan: It's been hurting since the first day
Karthik: I know. I just keep thinking, what if they find something? Then I have to deal with it, and the demo, and the viva
Chetan: And if you don't go, the ache stays and you still have to deal with everything
Karthik: That's why I don't want to hear what they say
Chetan: Book it tonight. I'll sit with you at the clinic
Karthik: Ok. Ok. Tomorrow morning I'll call 😔
Chetan: Tonight.

qa.q: Which event did Karthik give as the reason for waiting after the first delay?
qa.a: The demo on Thursday, and then the viva next week.

qa.q: What is Karthik afraid of, according to the chat?
qa.a: Karthik does not want to hear what the doctors will say, so fear of bad news sits under the busy excuses.

qa.q: What could Karthik do to break the pattern of postponing, and why would it work?
qa.a: Karthik could book the appointment right away for a slot after the deadlines, because a fixed time turns a vague someday into a plan and Chetan's company makes it easier to face. 🙂

qa.q: How does Chetan see Karthik's delay?
qa.a: Chetan sees weeks slipping by with the pain unchanged and Karthik more stressed, so Chetan keeps pushing for a booking while offering to come along.

grounding: A student keeps postponing a check-up out of fear and workload, and the delay adds stress.
